title: A body-only save keeps pictures the previous version mapped from local file names
description:
Bug-fix story. Evidence (Machines on Machines story-development session, Papyrus 5.108.0): on content-item-what-if-ai-wrote-just-the-bass-line-9acd2e3bba926bef a body-only save (v14) whose body names pictures by local file name (::image{src="earworm.png" srcDark="earworm.dark.png"}, front matter image: earworm.png, which is how the editing agents write drafts) saved with no warning. Publish then refused with image-missing earworm.png. Re-saving with --images pics worked (v15): every file came back image-unchanged and it published.

Cause: carry-forward (_carry_media_forward / referenced_media_paths() in src/papyrus_content/story_reporting.py, from PR #1456) matches only stored asset paths, not the local names the previous save mapped them from.

Two defects, both fixed properly (no workaround, no fallback):
1. Carry-forward resolves local file names (body src and srcDark, and front matter image) through the previous version recorded name-to-stored-path mapping, and carries every resolved picture (light and dark) forward.
2. A save whose body or front matter names a picture that is neither supplied with --images nor resolvable from the previous version is refused at save time with a message naming the file; no version is written. Publish is no longer where this is caught.

Related: PPY-732228 (carry-forward srcDark, closed), PPY-e9f8ac (save-version MediaAsset rows), PPY-5978b4, PPY-a96347.

Testing: must be exercised on a Story whose previous version came from save-version --images (not only on stored-path bodies), since that is the case that failed.

Gherkin:
Feature: Body-only saves keep pictures named by local file name
  Scenario: Body-only save with local names carries every picture forward and the story publishes
    Given a Story whose previous version was saved with --images and mapped earworm.png and earworm.dark.png to stored paths
    When I save a new version with only a changed body that names earworm.png and earworm.dark.png
    Then the save succeeds with no warning
    And the new version carries both pictures
    And publishing the Story succeeds
  Scenario: Front matter image named by local file name is carried forward
    Given a Story whose previous version was saved with --images and mapped earworm.png to a stored path
    When I save a body-only version whose front matter says image: earworm.png
    Then the new version carries the picture and publishing succeeds
  Scenario: Light and dark names both resolve
    Given the previous version mapped a light name and its dark name
    When a body-only save names both in an image directive
    Then both stored files are carried and neither is reported missing
  Scenario: A save naming an unknown file is refused up front
    Given a Story whose previous version has no mapping for missing.png
    When I save a body that names missing.png and supply no --images
    Then the save is refused with a message naming missing.png
    And no new version is written
  Scenario: Unknown dark name is refused up front
    When a save names a known light file and an unmapped dark file
    Then the save is refused naming the dark file and no version is written
  Scenario: Unknown front matter image is refused up front
    When a save sets front matter image to an unmapped file
    Then the save is refused naming the file and no version is written
